manifest.name: dsh-liquid-inference
manifest.description: Liquid Inference for DeepSeek Harness: a `liquid` model route plus read-only market tools

scripts.check: pnpm run typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm run build && pnpm run test:install

capability.invocation: call the liquid_get_routers tool with no arguments
capability.expected: returns an array of router models that includes liquid.auto

bundle.text:
# Layer applied when a profile lists this bundle.
#
# 1. `llm-pi-ai` is mounted dormant by @deepseek-ai/dsh-base; supplying a
#    `liquid` provider profile registers the route. Liquid speaks OpenAI Chat
#    Completions at /v1, so no custom adapter is needed. The key resolves per
#    request from LIQUID_API_KEY; `x-liquid-cap-usd` locks the most any one
#    request can cost, before the first token. Set LIQUID_CAP_USD to change it.
#    A patch replaces the row's whole `config`, so another bundle's pi-ai
#    providers must be restated in the profile's own cordis.patch.yml.
# 2. `liquid-tools` mounts the read-only market tools.
#
# Router ranking suffixes (:premium, :balanced, :economy, :cheapest) are
# documented in the description of GET /v1/exchange/routers. Reasoning levels
# are sent as `reasoning_effort`; the exchange passes the level through
# unchecked, so a level the winning provider rejects fails that request.
- id: llm-pi-ai
  config:
    providers:
      liquid:
        displayName: Liquid Inference
        api: openai-completions
        baseURL: https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1
        apiKeyEnv: LIQUID_API_KEY
        headers:
          x-liquid-cap-usd: !!js process.env.LIQUID_CAP_USD ?? '1'
        models:
          - id: liquid.auto
            name: Liquid Auto
            contextWindow: 10000000
            maxTokens: 1048576
            input: [text, image]
            reasoningEfforts: { off: , low: low, medium: medium, high: high }
          - id: liquid.auto:cheapest
            name: Liquid Auto (cheapest)
            contextWindow: 10000000
            maxTokens: 1048576
            input: [text, image]
            reasoningEfforts: { off: , low: low, medium: medium, high: high }
          - id: liquid.auto:economy
            name: Liquid Auto (economy)
            contextWindow: 10000000
            maxTokens: 1048576
            input: [text, image]
            reasoningEfforts: { off: , low: low, medium: medium, high: high }
          - id: liquid.auto:balanced
            name: Liquid Auto (balanced)
            contextWindow: 10000000
            maxTokens: 1048576
            input: [text, image]
            reasoningEfforts: { off: , low: low, medium: medium, high: high }
          - id: liquid.auto:premium
            name: Liquid Auto (premium)
            contextWindow: 10000000
            maxTokens: 1048576
            input: [text, image]
            reasoningEfforts: { off: , low: low, medium: medium, high: high }
          - id: deepseek-v4-flash
            name: DeepSeek V4 Flash (via Liquid)
            contextWindow: 1048576
            maxTokens: 65536
            reasoningEfforts: { off: , low: low, medium: medium, high: high }

- insert:
    - id: liquid-tools
      name: dsh-liquid-inference

readme.text: [Liquid Inference](https://liquidinference.ai) for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): a `liquid` model route plus read-only market tools.

Not published to npm yet. Install from GitHub or from a packed tarball, then export a buyer key with the `spend` scope and restart the profile:

```sh
export LIQUID_API_KEY=sk-liquid-...
```

**From GitHub.** The built `lib/` is committed, so no build step or `allowBuilds` entry is needed:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:architect-xyz/liquid-dsh-plugin
```

Pin a commit (`github:architect-xyz/liquid-dsh-plugin#<sha>`) so a later push cannot change what you install.

**From a tarball.** Needs no build permission:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/architect-xyz/liquid-dsh-plugin.git
cd liquid-dsh-plugin && pnpm install && pnpm pack
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-liquid-inference-0.1.0.tgz
```

Pick **Liquid Auto** (`liquid.auto`) in the model picker.

**Model route `liquid`** — no adapter code. The bundle patch configures the stock `llm-pi-ai` adapter with `api: openai-completions`, `baseURL: https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1` and `apiKeyEnv: LIQUID_API_KEY`.

- **Cap.** Each request carries `x-liquid-cap-usd`, the most it can cost, locked before the first token. The default is 1 USD; set `LIQUID_CAP_USD` in the launching environment to change it.
- **Models.** `liquid.auto` plus its ranking variants `:cheapest`, `:economy`, `:balanced` and `:premium` (documented in the description of `GET /v1/exchange/routers`), and `deepseek-v4-flash` as a pinned model. Add any id from `GET /v1/models` with a `models` entry in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.
- **Reasoning.** Levels `low`, `medium` and `high` are sent as `reasoning_effort`. The exchange passes the level through unchecked, so a level the winning provider rejects fails that request.

**Tools** (plugin `liquid-inference`)

| Tool | Endpoint | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `liquid_get_book` | `GET /v1/exchange/offers` | no |
| `liquid_get_markets` | `GET /v1/exchange/markets` | no |
| `liquid_get_routers` | `GET /v1/exchange/routers` | no |
| `liquid_get_job` | `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` | yes |

Chat, image, speech and video purchases are deliberately not tools: the harness's own model route is the one place that spends.

Full prompts and tool results go to `router.inference.ai.exchange`, which forwards them to whichever third-party provider wins the auction. The key is read per request, from the credential store when the profile mounts one and from `LIQUID_API_KEY` otherwise (headless profiles disable the store). It is never written to config.

- The patch replaces the `llm-pi-ai` row's whole `config`. If another bundle also configures pi-ai providers, restate them in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.
- Develop: `pnpm install && pnpm run check`. Commit the rebuilt `lib/` with source changes (CI fails on a stale one). `pnpm run test:install` packs the bundle, installs the tarball into an isolated profile of a real dsh (`DSH_VERSION` picks the release, default `next`) and boots it; it needs network access.
